question: What is the real cache-line straddler rate at LiteInst syscall patch sites across a corpus of real binaries, and does it warrant per-machine calibration of the WordPatch++ staleness wait?
method: Static, decoder-independent. For every decoded `syscall` (0f 05) instruction in a corpus of system ELF binaries and shared libraries, compute (virtual_address mod 64). ELF load bases are page-aligned (4096 % 64 == 0), so (runtime_addr mod 64) == (vaddr mod 64): ASLR does not change the cache-line offset, making the static vaddr exact for the runtime classification.

classification.word8_straddler: classify_word_patch() selects GuardedSplit iff the 8-byte WordPatch++ publication word [addr, addr+8) crosses a 64-byte line, i.e. (addr mod 64) in 57..63. This is the OPERATIVE rule that drives bail-to-ptrace / needs-calibrated-wait on the Concurrent publication path.
classification.prefix2_straddler: The reported end-of-run `cacheline_straddlers` stat counts sites whose straddle_after is Some, where straddle_after = split_offset(addr, min(instr_len, 5)). For a 2-byte `syscall` this fires ONLY at offset 63. This is a diagnostic sub-statistic, NOT the bail rule.

command: bash scan.sh corpus.txt out   # corpus = 1459 unique realpath ELF files from /usr/bin,/bin,/usr/lib64,/lib64
caps: files > 40 MiB skipped (30 files: giant Go/internal monoliths e.g. devfeature 1.08 GB, libLLVM), per-objdump timeout 25s. See skipped.csv.
